purpose: Research index of extremist and hate-group organizations for comparative study. It is not a universal census. Labels are source-dependent and membership counts are included only where a credible source provides an estimate.
classification_guardrail: A group is not classified as hateful merely because it is controversial, religious, political or unpopular. The dataset records the classification used by the named source and keeps source and category attached to the record.

records.name: Ku Klux Klan
records.membership_count_note: No single authoritative current membership figure; different Klan organizations report or are estimated differently.
records.description: Historically significant U.S. white-supremacist organization founded after the Civil War. The name has been used by multiple successive organizations rather than one continuously identical legal body.

records.name: Nation of Islam
records.category: religious-political movement; classification varies by source
records.origin_or_headquarters: Detroit, Michigan; national headquarters in Chicago, Illinois, USA
records.membership_count_note: Public membership estimates vary substantially and should not be treated as a census.
records.description: African-American religious and political movement founded in Detroit in 1930. It should not automatically be placed in a hate-group category without specifying the source and criteria.

records.name: Active Club network
records.membership_count_note: No reliable global membership census located; SPLC documents numerous local chapters/locations.
records.description: Decentralized network of local white-nationalist fitness-oriented groups. Treat chapter count and participant estimates separately from formal membership.

records.name: American Freedom Party
records.membership_count_note: No reliable current membership census located.
records.description: White-nationalist political organization documented in U.S. extremist-group research.

records.name: Aryan Brotherhood
records.origin_or_headquarters: San Quentin State Prison, California, USA
records.membership_count_note: Membership figures are disputed and organization is fragmented; use law-enforcement estimates with dates when available.
records.description: White-supremacist prison gang that emerged at San Quentin in the 1960s and later developed networks beyond the prison system.

records.name: Blood & Honour
records.membership_count_note: No authoritative global census; local organizations vary over time.
records.description: International white-power music and political network originating in the United Kingdom.

records.name: Combat 18
records.membership_count_note: No reliable current global membership census.
records.description: Militant neo-Nazi network that emerged in Britain in the early 1990s and became associated with violent extremist activity.

records.name: National Action
records.membership_count_note: No current legal membership census; the organization itself is proscribed in the UK.
records.description: British neo-Nazi organization proscribed under UK terrorism legislation in 2016.

records.name: Atomwaffen Division
records.membership_count_note: Estimates vary; no reliable current worldwide census.
records.description: Neo-Nazi accelerationist network associated with violent extremist ideology. Later successor and affiliated networks should be tracked separately.

records.name: The Base
records.description: Transnational accelerationist neo-Nazi network. The record should distinguish the original organization from later cells and aliases.

records.name: Hammerskins
records.origin_or_headquarters: Dallas, Texas, USA; later international chapters
records.description: International white-power skinhead network founded in the United States and expanded through regional chapters.

records.name: Proud Boys
records.category: far-right extremist organization; classification varies by jurisdiction/source
records.origin_or_headquarters: New York City, New York, USA
records.membership_count_note: Public membership estimates are uncertain and should be time-stamped if used.
records.description: Male-only far-right organization founded in New York in 2016. Its classification and organizational status have changed across jurisdictions and over time.

records.name: Heil Hitler / Nazi organizations historical cluster
records.membership_count_note: Not a single organization; never use this record as a membership count.
records.description: Placeholder category for historical and successor neo-Nazi organizations; individual organizations must be recorded separately before quantitative comparison.

counting_note: The project should prefer three separate metrics: organizations identified, chapters/locations identified, and people estimated. These are not interchangeable. For example, SPLC's U.S. extremist maps enumerate groups/locations, not a universal count of individual members.
research_sources: Southern Poverty Law Center extremist files
U.S. Department of State designations where applicable
